Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Over 23 years, did the Quran contradict itself?

Read closely, says the Quran: a text not from God would show much inconsistency. What holds, what critics say.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَـٰفًا كَثِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then do they not reflect upon the Qur’ān?[203] If it had been from [any] other than Allāh, they would have found within it much contradiction.

Translator's notes

[203] i.e., its meanings and its objective.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:82

Translation

“Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him. Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

Original · Hebrew

כָּל־אִמְרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃ אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃

Proverbs · 30:5-6

World English Bible

Any long project changes as it goes: a person who writes for twenty years does not say at the end what they said at the start. So the fair test of a text given over about twenty-three years, in the traditional account, is not whether it varies, but whether it contradicts itself, above all at the centre. The Quran sets that test itself: if it were from other than God, people would find much inconsistency in it. Elsewhere it says it has no crookedness at all (18:1).

A question for you

Where would you look for a contradiction in a long text?

If you sayIn the details: dates, numbers, wording of the same story.
ThenCritics do look there, and the app does not hide those cases. Detail varies in any long text, so the question is whether it touches the centre.
If you sayIn the centre: what it says about God, justice and the person.
ThenThat is the test the verse sets. The last part of this Step looks at what stays constant.
If you sayIn the laws, which seem to change.
ThenThe Quran itself speaks of replacing one verse with a better or an equal. Scholars discuss which rulings and why, and the app does not rule on it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ ۖ وَرَتَّلْنَـٰهُ تَرْتِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.[1023]

Translator's notes

[1023] Also, "recited it with distinct recitation."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:32

﴿وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَـٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَـٰهُ تَنزِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [it is] a Qur’ān which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down progressively.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:106

A book written in one sitting can be polished by one hand. This one was given in parts, as events unfolded, and the Quran says why: to steady the listener's heart, and so that it could be recited slowly to people. The objectors asked why it did not come all at once. The book records the question and answers it. That makes consistency harder, not easier, because each part was heard by real people as it came.

A question for you

How would you test a text given in parts over many years?

If you sayRead it in the order it was given.
ThenScholars do this and see development in tone from the earlier chapters to the later ones. The question is whether the message develops or breaks.
If you sayRead it as a whole and look for what recurs.
ThenThat is the next part: what recurs, and how the parts are put together.
If you sayI would look for what its critics have found.
ThenA good test, and it is the one the verse invites. The strongest cases are named at the end of this Step.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ كِتَـٰبًا مُّتَشَـٰبِهًا مَّثَانِىَ تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance [i.e., mention] of Allāh. That is the guidance of Allāh by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allāh sends astray - for him there is no guide.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:23

Translation

Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.

Original · Hebrew

אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃

Proverbs · 28:14

World English Bible

Look for the centre. Across the chapters the same few things return: one God, accountability, mercy, justice. The forms change with the setting: a short rhythmic address, a long legal passage, a story. This verse describes the book as alike in its parts and paired, returning to its themes. Scholars of different faiths also find that many chapters are built with care, themes echoing in patterns. Some of those patterns are debated.

A question for you

What would count, for you, as a contradiction at the centre?

If you sayTwo opposite teachings about God.
ThenThat is the right place to look. Read how the book speaks of God across its chapters and judge.
If you sayA command that cancels another.
ThenThe Quran speaks of replacing a verse. The question is whether the centre shifts. Scholars discuss which rulings were replaced, and the app does not rule on it.
If you sayI would need to read it all.
ThenHonest, and the best test. The verse asks for exactly that.
